newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Bossi to face trial for incitement.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Bossi to face trial for incitement.

text.p: An Italian judge on Monday ordered separatist Northern League leader Umberto Bossi to stand trial for urging his supporters at a political rally to "identify and pursue" far-right voters.
Judge Mariarosa Persico ruled in the north-eastern town of Tolmezzo that Bossi should stand trial on charges of "incitement to violence, aggravated threats and defamation."
The trial was set for March 27, 1998.
Bossi, who did not attend the preliminary hearing in Tolmezzo on Monday, is due to be tried on similar charges by a court in the northern town of Bergamo on July 2.
Members of the far-right National Alliance (AN) party took action against Bossi after the Northern League leader made his remarks at a rally near Tolmezzo in August 1995.
Bossi was widely reported by Italian media to have told his supporters to "identify and pursue house by house the members and supporters of National Alliance" whom he also called "dirty fascists".
Bossi has already been sentenced to eight months in another court case involving illegal party financing.

He was found guilty of accepting some 200 million lire ($118,000) in bribes for use by the League in its 1992 electoral campaign. The appeals court last week upheld the sentence, which now goes to the court of cassation, Italy's highest court.
"If you ask me, I think they have repression in mind," Bossi said on Monday after he was ordered to trial.
Bossi, whose League wants independence for Italy's rich north, has declared a northern state of "Padania".

Public derision at the League's perceived "antics" has shifted towards real concern since eight separatist paramilitaries occupied the bell tower in the lagoon city of Venice last month to publicise a drive for an independent Venetian republic.
The eight, who are now on trial, are not directly associated with the League but Bossi's opponents have argued that his secessionist rhetoric has incited hotheads.
